why: The words that make an environment variable's name look like it holds a credential. Redaction is the one place where being wrong in one direction is free and being wrong in the other prints a live token, so this record over-matches on purpose: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS holds a path and is redacted anyway. The `(^|[-_])…($|[-_])` boundaries are what keep TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM and WELES_KEYWORD_ROOT out while HF_TOKEN and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are caught. The alternative — an allowlist of credential-shaped names that are actually safe — prints a secret the first time somebody adds an entry wrong.
boundaries_why: A name part, not a substring: the word must start the name or follow a separator, and end the name or precede one.
